chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And He made me blessed wherever I was,' he said: 'Beneficial (to the people).'

key_terms.أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُ: Wherever I was (indicating ubiquity of the blessing)
key_terms.مُبَارَكاً: Blessed (adjective describing the state of being blessed)
key_terms.نَفَّاعاً: Beneficial (the interpretation of 'blessed' in this context)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'blessed' mean in the context of Prophet Isa's statement?
ai.summary: In this concise exegesis from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the term 'mubarakan' (blessed) in Surah Maryam 19:31 as 'naffaan' (beneficial), linking divine blessing directly to tangible utility for humanity. This interpretation underscores a core Shia theological principle that true spiritual status is manifested through active service and benefit to the community, a concept that resonates with the chapter's theme of advising and aiding the Muslims.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [19:31] And He has Made me (Isaas) Blessed wherever I may be: Heasws said: ‘Beneficial (to the people)’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yahya ibn al- Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy: ‘. . . He has blessed me no matter where I dwell, . . .’ [19:31] the Imam said, ‘“Blessed” means, the most beneficial to people.’”
